subject: Trace & Retention: bundling matrix and discount variance
body:
From: Lina Perez <lina.perez@acmeops.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acmeops.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify bundling matrix & discount variance for tracing/retention/dashboard add-ons

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the dashboards look promising. Before we move to an internal approval, I need a clearer view of how Redwood applies discounts across the observability add-ons. Specifically:

- If we commit to a 12-month reserved capacity for Hosted inference, how do discounts stack across: retention (30/90/365 days), tracing (sampled vs full), and advanced dashboards (seat vs project)?
- Is there a single bundle price with a blended discount, or are discounts applied per SKU?
- For a 3-month pilot (no annual commit), do you have a pilot price or credits we can apply toward the first invoice?

Can you send the matrix and call out any non-linear breakpoints (e.g., jumps at 10TB, 25TB) and whether trace ingest caps change price bands? An example workbook would help.

—Lina
Operations Lead, Acme Ops

---

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Perez <lina.perez@acmeops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify bundling matrix & discount variance for tracing/retention/dashboard add-ons

Lina — thanks for the note and great question. I attached a draft workbook that maps our SKU bands to commit tiers and shows where discounts apply. Highlights below, then a quick follow-up on pilot terms. Attachment: observability_pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx (workbook with scenarios).

Quick summary:
- Discount model: discounts are primarily applied at the bundle/commit level rather than per-SKU. We offer two stacking behaviors: 1) bundle-blend (all add-ons combined under a single commit for a blended discount) and 2) SKU carve (customers may elect to commit to specific SKUs and receive discounts only on committed SKUs).
- Breakpoints: retention (30/90/365) has price breakpoints at 5TB, 15TB, 40TB. Tracing ingest has breakpoints at 1TB, 5TB, 12TB where sampled vs full collection affects effective price per event. Dashboards: seat-based discounts apply starting at 10 seats and change again at 50 seats (project-level packages can alter this).
- Pilot policy: for a 3-month pilot we typically provide a $25k credit toward observability add-ons for new customers, or a 50% pilot rate on dash seats for up to 3 months. Credits are bill-applied and require a short SOW.

Callouts in the workbook you should check:
1) The blended bundle example (Tab: BundleBlend) models a 20% blended discount at a 12-month commit of $120k/year across inference + retention + tracing.
2) The SKU carve example (Tab: SKUCarve) shows a case where committing only to retention yields a 12% discount on retention while tracers remain at list unless committed separately.
3) We include overage smoothing options (monthly cap and pre-bucket) — see notes column in each band.

Next steps I propose: 1) Lina, confirm the rough expected retention volume and seats; 2) Ben, could you run a short concession check for the $25k credit versus a 10% list discount on a $100k observability add-on ask?

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify bundling matrix & discount variance for tracing/retention/dashboard add-ons

Looping in finance considerations. Quick notes:
- $25k pilot credit vs 10% discount: which preserves ARR and is easier for ACME procurement? Credit is one-off and shows on invoice as credit; discount reduces recognition and may complicate our revenue bands. For this size I'd recommend credit if the goal is trial-to-convert.
- If ACME is likely to move to a 12-month commit at $120k+, we can offer a 12% bundle discount plus the pilot credit for a limited window (requires legal sign-off).

I can approve the $25k credit for pilot under the following constraints: written SOW, pilot scope limited to 3 months, and a 30-day notice for any downgrade. If they want a permanent list discount instead, bring it to me with the modeled ARR impact.

Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

---

From: Lina Perez <lina.perez@acmeops.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acmeops.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify bundling matrix & discount variance for tracing/retention/dashboard add-ons

Thanks Sofia and Ben — this is exactly what we needed. A few clarifying items from our procurement/legal side: 

- We prefer a pilot credit (simpler) but need that to be explicitly non-recurring and expiry-dated. Can you include the credit language in the SOW?
- For the 12-month commit example: can you provide two scenarios in the workbook — (A) commit to retention + dashboards only, (B) commit to full bundle including tracing — and show net ARR and year-1 cashflow impact (invoice + credit).
- Which SLAs apply to advanced dashboards (RTO for query, data freshness)? Our SRE team will want those in the SOW.

If you can send an updated workbook and a short SOW draft with the pilot-credit clause, we can route to procurement.

—Lina

Attachments mentioned: none in this reply.

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Perez <lina.perez@acmeops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify bundling matrix & discount variance for tracing/retention/dashboard add-ons

Lina — attaching the updated workbook and a short SOW draft. Key changes: added Scenarios A/B with year-1 cashflow sheets, explicit pilot-credit clause (expires 90 days from execution; non-recurring; applied to first invoice). SLAs for dashboards (Tab: SLAs) list a 30s median query RTO, 99.9% availability for dashboard rendering, and 5-minute guaranteed ingest-to-visualization freshness for standard pipelines (we can tighten for an add-on SLA at an incremental fee). Attachment: redwood_observability_proposal_ACME.pdf (SOW draft + commercial terms).

If this looks right I'll loop legal to generate the SOW signature packet. Ben — this is the ask for concession approval: $25k pilot credit on top of a 12% bundle discount for a 12-month commit >= $120k ARR. Naomi, please flag any revenue recognition concerns.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call if procurement wants to review the SOW.

Best,
Sofia

[Attachments: observability_pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx (workbook), redwood_observability_proposal_ACME.pdf (SOW draft)]
